blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Food Safety & Food Retail. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Food retail carries the consumer-facing safety duty: fresh-chain quality, supplier verification, recall readiness and waste economics. Telemetry and traceability turn compliance cost into customer trust and margin.

The pattern composes Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust, Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Cold-chain management, Supplier verification, Recall response) on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel. Governance inherits the sector frame — Food-safety regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Contracts as production software: specification, formal verification and audit before value moves.
Proof, not paperwork: EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Agriculture & Food Systems level this capability reads as: geolocation-anchored plots, custody events and regulator interfaces (due-diligence evidence produced continuously). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
